To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the addition of stress imaging (PET MPI, SPECT MPI, or stress echocardiographic wall motion studies) to clinical data improves the diagnostic and prognostic value in the management of patients with suspected or known CAD, and that the prognostic power of stress imaging in this patient population is comparable with that of clinical data.

(1) the prognostic accuracy of stress imaging is superior to the prognostic power of the traditional clinical risk factors and (2) the prognostics value of the stress imaging is superior for the assessment of CAD in women and in patients with a normal or near normal resting left ventricular (LV) function.
the prognostic performance of stress MPI is not affected by the use of the new generation of SPECT MPI cameras.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the assessment of the prognostic and diagnostic value of cardiovascular imaging, with the ultimate goal to provide physicians and payers with the necessary tools to select the best imaging test for a given patient.
the development and application of statistical models to the assessment of cardiovascular imaging, in order to evaluate its clinical value and application.
the assessment of the prognostic and diagnostic value of cardiovascular imaging.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, although the prognostic information provided by cardiovascular imaging is not as strong as that provided by clinical risk factors, the prognostic impact of cardiovascular imaging is significant and independent.
the prognostic and clinical value of cardiovascular imaging is well established for stress MPI and stress echocardio-graphy.
the current evidence base does not support a role for stress CT or stress CMR in the evaluation of patients with known CAD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the near future, we will be able to identify the patients who will not benefit from revascularization, and those who will, with high certainty.
, in general, the prognostic accuracy of cardiovascular imaging is high and the results are comparable to those obtained with the traditional risk stratification models, such as the Framingham score.

, in the future, cardiovascular imaging will have to be based on the following premises: 1) the use of a validated imaging modality for the specific indication, 2) the application of the appropriate imaging protocol, and 3) the use of the most appropriate image interpretation method.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the prognostic performance of the different modalities should be assessed in the same patient cohort, using similar end-points and a similar follow-up duration.

the clinical value and cost-effectiveness of cardiovascular imaging are not necessarily related, and that the latter is not the only factor that determines the future reimbursement for cardiovascular imaging studies.
the use of stress MPI, whether by SPECT, PET, or CMR, is associated with improved survival, and this benefit is independent of the presence or severity of CAD.
